name: Graham's pebbling conjecture: pebbling number of the square of the Lemke graph pi(L box L)
compute_profile: laptop-days to needs cluster (unmeasured research estimate for discovery and exact certification on 64 vertices); existing small-graph calibrations do not establish full-search feasibility
statement: In graph pebbling (Chung 1989), a pebbling move removes two pebbles from one vertex and places one pebble on an adjacent vertex. The pebbling number pi(G) of a connected graph G is the minimum p such that from every distribution of p pebbles on V(G) and every root r in V(G), some sequence of moves puts a pebble on r. Trivially pi(G) >= |V(G)| (placing 1 pebble on each vertex except r leaves no moves). Ronald Graham (1989) conjectured that pi(G box H) <= pi(G) * pi(H) for all connected graphs under the Cartesian product. Graphs satisfying the 2-pebbling property obey Graham's conjecture against many graph classes. Paul Lemke (Lemke & Kleitman 1989) discovered the 8-vertex, 13-edge graph L (House of Graphs 51416; V = {0..7}, edges (0,1),(0,7),(1,6),(2,5),(2,6),(2,7),(3,5),(3,6),(3,7),(4,5),(4,6),(4,7),(5,7), |Aut(L)| = 6) with pi(L) = 8 that fails the 2-pebbling property: specifically, there are 5 distributions with p = 12 pebbles on q = 5 occupied vertices (so p + q = 17 > 2*pi(L) = 16) that cannot place 2 pebbles on root 1. Thus L box L (64 vertices, 208 edges, |Aut(L box L)| = 72, 21 vertex orbits) is a primary candidate counterexample to Graham's conjecture (which predicts pi(L box L) = 64 vs >= 65). Known upper bounds progressed from 128 (Chung / Pachter-Snevily-Voxman 1995) to 108 (Hurlbert, arXiv:1101.5641 / J. Comb. Optim. 34, 2017) to 91 (Kenter & Skipper 2018) to 85 (Kenter, Skipper, and Wilson, arXiv:1905.08683 / Theoretical Computer Science 803, 2020, computed via floating-point Gurobi MILP; Footnote 3 notes it was not verified by an exact rational IP solver). Flocco, Pulaj, and Yerger (arXiv:2312.12618 / Discrete Applied Mathematics 347, 2024) gave hand-verifiable tree-strategy weight certificates for pi(L box L) <= 96, and Pulaj, Wood, and Yerger (arXiv:2411.19314, Nov 2024) used bilevel MILP (floating-point CPLEX) to prove pi_4(L' box L'') <= 64 for all 8-vertex minimal Lemke products when restricted to pebble supports of size |Supp(D)| <= 4. The unrestricted range 64 <= pi(L box L) <= 85 remains open. Hurlbert offered a reward for resolving the 64-pebble question in footnote 2 of the published Weight Function Lemma paper. The current terms are unverified.
success_criterion: CONFIRMED: EITHER (a) a counterexample establishing pi(L box L) >= 65: an explicit distribution D of 64 pebbles on V(L box L) = {0..7} x {0..7} (necessarily of support |Supp(D)| >= 5 unless also refuting arXiv:2411.19314's floating-point CPLEX bound) and root r = (u_r, v_r), together with a machine-checkable unreachability proof (an explicit valid pebbling weight-function/potential certificate checked in exact rational arithmetic, an exact complete reachability certificate, or a Lean 4 proof with no sorry and axioms restricted to propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice); OR (b) an upper-bound proof establishing pi(L box L) <= 64 across all 21 automorphism orbits of roots in L box L, certified by exact rational (Fraction / SCIP-VIPR / SMT-checked) weight-function branch-and-bound certificates or a Lean 4 proof. Calibration: independently verify |E(L)| = 13, |Aut(L)| = 6, |Aut(L box L)| = 72 (21 vertex orbits), pi(L) = 8, and all five (p, q) = (12, 5) 2-pebbling failures on L (such as (0,0,1,1,1,7,0,2) targeting root 1). Recheck all cited primary papers and later primary literature at claim time: neither an already published counterexample nor an already established bound qualifies. A solver status or VIPR certificate for an incomplete model does not suffice; verify the complete reduction from pebbling reachability and every case-cover obligation.

partial_wins.statement: A certified exact-rational / SCIP-VIPR / Lean 4 upper-bound proof establishing pi(L box L) <= 75 across all 21 root orbits of L box L (strictly below Kenter-Skipper-Wilson's 85). The bound must also be strictly smaller than the strongest comparable published unrestricted bound at claim time. Matching the published bound of 85 with a new exact certificate is calibration, not a partial win. Do not count a full win twice.

verification_method: Pin the 8-vertex Lemke graph L with V = {0..7} and edges [(0,1),(0,7),(1,6),(2,5),(2,6),(2,7),(3,5),(3,6),(3,7),(4,5),(4,6),(4,7),(5,7)] (House of Graphs 51416), and build the Cartesian product L box L where (u1,v1) ~ (u2,v2) iff (u1=u2 and v1~v2) or (v1=v2 and u1~u2). For an upper bound pi(L box L) <= U: verify that the finite root/case cover spans all 21 vertex orbits of Aut(L box L) (or all 64 roots), and check every leaf certificate in exact rational arithmetic (Python fractions.Fraction, VIPR exact rational IP checker, or Lean 4) using Hurlbert's Weight Function Lemma / tree-strategy potential inequalities. For a lower bound (unreachability of r from D): verify sum(D) = 64, D(r) = 0, and check the exact rational potential/invariant or Lean 4 proof ruling out every legal pebbling move sequence to r. Artifacts > 1 MB follow SUBMIT.md section 1. Check the encoding and finite case coverage as well as exact arithmetic in each solver certificate; VIPR validates the stated integer program, not the correctness of an unchecked pebbling reduction. Discovery and full verification runtimes have not been measured here.
angles: Exploit Aut(L box L) of order 72 and its 21 root orbits to search for exact upper-bound certificates improving the published bound of 85. Reproducing an exact certificate at 85 is a calibration step toward p1, not a bank win.

For a counterexample search (pi(L box L) >= 65), prioritize configurations with support size |Supp(D)| >= 5 (support <= 4 is reported <= 64 in arXiv:2411.19314, but using this as a complete exclusion requires checking its proof rather than trusting a floating-point solver) concentrated on vertices far from degree-2 root (1, 1) or (0, 0).
Test whether bilevel exact-SCIP + SMT (cvc5) verification (as proposed in arXiv:2411.19314 Section 5) closes larger support thresholds s >= 5.
pitfalls: Labeling convention pitfall: Kenter-Skipper-Wilson (2020) denote the original 13-edge Lemke graph (HoG 51416) as L (bound 85) and the other two minimal 8-vertex Lemke graphs as L_1, L_2 (bounds 84), whereas Flocco-Pulaj-Yerger (2024) and Pulaj-Wood-Yerger (2024) denote the original 13-edge Lemke graph HoG 51416 as L = L_1. Always pin by the explicit edge list above.
On the 8-vertex Lemke graph L itself, all five minimal 2-pebbling failures with p + q = 17 occur at (p, q) = (12, 5) targeting root 1 (zero failures exist at p = 9..11 or p = 13..16 with p + q = 17).

Cartesian product (box) vs tensor product: edges connect (u,v) to (u',v) for uu' in E(L) and to (u,v') for vv' in E(L). Naive BFS on 64-vertex L box L with 64 pebbles is intractable; unreachability claims require an exact potential/weight certificate or formal proof.
